newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Telecom earnings seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Telecom earnings seen rising.

text.p: Budget changes to reduce excise duty and inter-city call charges will boost Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd's (PTCL) earnings, according to a research report issued on Monday.

BMA Capital Management said in a report after Friday's government budget announcement that the blue-chip company's earnings would rise in fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) and rated the company a strong buy near 30 rupees.
"The (government's) 1997/98 budget brought good news for PTCL and its investors by announcing a reduction in excise duty on telephone calls to 25 percent from 40 percent," it said.
BMA said tariffs on inter-city calls would be reduced by 20 percent from July 1 to increase call volume.
"These measures are likely to help restore investor confidence in the stock and enhance prospects of its (PTCL's) strategic sale," the report added.
The report said PTCL was likely to revise its tariffs following the cut in excise duty.

"PTCL's gross tariff for local and international calls would remain the same for subscribers. But net tariffs are likely to increase by 12 percent for the PTCL because of the excise duty cut," Mudassar Malik, chief dealer at BMA, said.
This would result in higher revenue for PTCL in 1997/98, the report said. PTCL's earnings per share were expected to rise 23.76 percent in 1997/98 compared to 2.86 percent the previous year.
PTCL's after-tax profits fell to 6.595 billion rupees from 8.888 billion in the six months to December.

Excise duty on telephone calls had risen to 40 percent in the tax-laden 1996/97 government budget, and the Karachi Stock Exchange had asked the government to reduce it in the next budget to boost company profits and help the stock market.
PTCL was created on January 1, 1996 from state-controlled Pakistan Telecommunication Corporation.
Shares in PTCL, mostly owned by the government, gained 0.45 rupee, or 1.47 percent, to 31.10 on Monday at the Karachi bourse.
But Zaina Nowsherwan, a dealer at BMA Capital Management, said PTCL might dip on a correction in the short-term.
"PTCL gained sharply last week in a pre-budget rally and now, a correction is due. But the stock's mid- to long-term outlook remains positive after these budget announcements," she said.
She said the government had reduced its own revenue to boost that of PTCL, which would have a positive impact on stocks.
The report said the budgetary measures underlined the government's ability to influence PTCL's fortunes, even though PTCL was operating as an independent limited company.
In August 1994, the government sold three percent of PTCL's equity to the public at 30 rupees per share and nine percent at 55 rupees per share on the world market the following month.
